sections.h2: What should a seller know about Whiteside County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Whiteside County covers 697 square miles in northwestern Illinois, with the Mississippi River as its western boundary. Morrison is the county seat, and Sterling is the largest city. Rock Falls, Fulton and Prophetstown are the other cities, and villages include Albany, Erie, Lyndon and Tampico, the birthplace of a U.S. president.

The county was organized in 1836 from parts of Jo Daviess and Henry counties and has kept its boundaries ever since. Winters are cold: the Morrison January average runs from a low near 10 degrees to a high near 29, and July highs reach about 85.

Your bill depends on which of the county's 22 townships and which taxing districts cover the parcel, so a house in a city and a house on a township road can carry quite different totals even at the same assessed value.

sections.h2: How do Whiteside County home values and housing figures look?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Whiteside County was valued at $127,100 for 2020 to 2024, and 76.9% of homes are lived in by their owners.

sections.h2: Who collects and assesses property tax in Whiteside County?
sections.html:
The County Collector mails one bill per parcel and distributes the money to more than 140 taxing districts. For the 2024 taxes payable in 2025, the county collected $101,388,931.80, of which $98,835,123.12 was real estate tax.

  • Collector and Treasurer: 200 East Knox Street, Morrison, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., phone 815-772-5196.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: handles assessments, exemptions and address changes. The county site lists the office and its phone.
  • The Collector is not responsible for your assessment, the size of the bill, exemptions or a change of address.

You get a bill even when a mortgage company pays the tax from escrow. The county has no mortgage information, so questions about escrow go to your lender. An address change goes on the Tax Bill Change of Address Form, mailed to the Supervisor of Assessments.

sections.h2: When are Whiteside County tax bills due?
sections.html:
Whiteside County splits the bill into two installments, one in June and one in September. The county's 2026 calendar had bills mailed May 15, the first installment due June 17 and the second due September 1, with the penalty starting the next day for each. Mobile home tax was due June 1, 2026.

The county's 2026 calendar also listed the annual tax sale for November 5, 2026, which has passed. Dates shift from year to year, so read the calendar on the Collector's page for the current cycle.

Local taxing districts run on different fiscal years. Municipalities start May 1, school districts July 1 and the county December 1, and the tax roll and bills follow the levy ordinances those bodies adopt. Delinquencies pass to the State's Attorney and County Treasurer, and tax buyers file for judgment and conduct the sales.

Payment has to match the bill. The office accepts no partial payments, and the amount must equal an installment as shown, or both installments together by the first due date. Include the tax stub with the payment, or the office may return it.

sections.h2: How do you pay Whiteside County property tax?
sections.html:
The Collector's payment sheet lists several routes, and each has its own cutoff.

  • In person at the courthouse Treasurer's office, 8:30 to 4:30.
  • By mail, where a postmark by the due date avoids the late penalty. The county is not responsible for lost mail.
  • Automatic ACH withdrawal on each due date, stopped only by a written request.
  • Credit card with a 2.25% convenience fee, or e-check with a $1.50 fee.
  • At participating banks, until the bank cutoff. The 2026 sheet gave September 1, 2026 as the last day.
  • In the drop box inside the Law Enforcement Center door at the Morrison courthouse, by 4:30 on the due date.

Make checks payable to the Whiteside County Collector. A returned check carries a $25.00 fee on top of penalties, and the office stops taking personal checks 30 days before the tax sale.

sections.h2: How does Whiteside County assess homes and handle appeals?
sections.html:
The county assesses each home at one-third of market value, which is 33.3%, and the tax bill comes from the final equalized assessed value less exemptions, times the tax rate. An equalization factor evens out levels across the county's 22 townships. Assessments look back over the previous three years of sales and use January 1 as the valuation day, so a falling market does not always lower your number right away.

If you think the assessment is too high, first compare it with an appraisal or recent sales of similar homes. Then contact the Supervisor of Assessments office. An appeal to the Board of Review has to be in writing within 30 days of the township's publication, a limit that mirrors 35 ILCS 200/16-55.

New construction raises the assessment, and the county gets copies of building permits and inspects. Illinois offers a home improvement exemption that lasts four years, capped at $25,000 of assessed value, and the adjustment appears on the tax bill.

sections.h2: What relief programs lower a Whiteside County bill?
sections.html:
Whiteside County is not next to a county of 3,000,000 residents, so the standard state dollar caps apply to its homestead exemptions.

  • General homestead exemption: up to $6,000 off equalized assessed value for an owner-occupied home (35 ILCS 200/15-175).
  • Senior citizens exemption: up to $5,000 for owners 65 or older (35 ILCS 200/15-170).
  • Low-income senior assessment freeze (35 ILCS 200/15-172). Ask the assessor for income limits.

If you think you qualify for an exemption and the bill does not show one, ask the Supervisor of Assessments. After a sale, the homestead exemption stays for the rest of that assessment year, and the assessor may ask the new owner to apply.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Whiteside County taxes, and how does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Past-due installments carry interest of 1 1/2% per month or part of a month in counties of fewer than 3,000,000 people (35 ILCS 200/21-15). A mailed payment postmarked by the due date is not delinquent.

Unpaid taxes can end up at the annual tax sale. After a sale, the owner may redeem before three years pass from the date of sale, subject to exceptions in 35 ILCS 200/21-350.

  • Ask the Collector for the amount due on the parcel, with penalty, before you sign a contract.
  • Have the closing agent pay the balance from your proceeds.
  • If the parcel was sold at the tax sale, ask about redemption cost and timing before closing.

Late bills, an old address or an inherited house can all hide a balance, so check the parcel by number rather than by name.

faqs.q: When are Whiteside County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments, one in June and one in September. In 2026 they were due June 17 and September 1. Read the Collector's page for the dates in the current cycle.

faqs.q: What does it cost to pay Whiteside County taxes by card?
faqs.a: A 2.25% convenience fee applies to credit cards, and e-checks cost $1.50. Paying by check, in person or by ACH withdrawal avoids a card fee.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial payment in Whiteside County?
faqs.a: No. The county takes only a full installment as printed on the bill, or both installments together by the first due date.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Whiteside County assessment?
faqs.a: Send a written appeal to the Board of Review within 30 days of the township publication. Gather an appraisal or sales of comparable homes first, and ask the Supervisor of Assessments office with any questions.

faqs.q: What if I sell a Whiteside County house with taxes unpaid?
faqs.a: Get a payoff from the Collector at 815-772-5196 and pay it from the sale proceeds. Interest of 1 1/2% per month keeps adding until the balance is paid, so settle it at closing.
